hits.snippet: Joby Aviation agreed to acquire Dayton-based Resonant Sciences for approximately $500 million, a deal that would give the electric-air-taxi developer a dedicated defense business with classified capabilities, a cleared workforce and expanded manufacturing capacity in Ohio. Joby said Resonant will continue operating under its existing name and leadership after the transaction closes, while becoming home to Joby’s defense aircraft and autonomy programs. Joby’s commercial organization will remain focused on certifying, manufacturing and commercializing its electric air-taxi business. The company said the transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory reviews and other customary closing conditions. ### Why it matters The deal would expand Joby’s presence in defense technology while preserving a separate focus for its commercial aviation business. hits.snippet: Joby Aviation announced on August 11, 2026, that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Resonant Sciences, a Dayton, Ohio-based defense technology company, for approximately $500 million. The deal gives the California eVTOL developer immediate scale in the defense sector through an already profitable business supporting active US national security programs. Founded in 2015, Resonant designs, manufactures and delivers radio frequency (RF) and mission systems for US national security customers and is a global leader in low-observability technologies, structures and subsystems. hits.title: Joby Aviation acquires defense tech startup Resonant Sciences for $500 million as it expands beyond air taxis - Tech Startups
hits.snippet: The electric air taxi maker said Tuesday it has agreed to acquire Ohio-based defense technology startup Resonant Sciences for roughly $500 million, giving Joby a dedicated defense business at a time when military spending and demand for autonomous aircraft are rising. Joby expects to pay about $450 million in cash and $50 million in common stock. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027. Resonant Sciences designs, manufactures, and delivers advanced radio-frequency and mission systems for U.S. national security customers. Once the acquisition closes, Resonant will become Joby’s dedicated defense business, bringing together its existing operations with Joby’s hybrid aircraft and autonomy technologies. [...] The deal marks a significant shift for a company best known for developing electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft, or eVTOLs, for commercial passenger transportation. Joby’s commercial aircraft business will remain focused on electric air taxis, but the Resonant acquisition gives the company another route into a defense market that has become increasingly attractive to aviation startups. The acquisition will represent a significant expansion of Joby's defense business. The investment also strengthens ties between Joby and the Dayton area. Resonant Sciences has about 250 Dayton-area employees, most of them in Beavercreek.
